hints: Include a constant term before the two linear fractions: A+B/(x+2a)+C/(x+3a).
Clear denominators, find all constants, and recombine to check the original numerator.
walkthrough:
Expand the denominator of $f(x)$:
$$(x + 2a)(x + 3a) = x^2 + 3ax + 2ax + 6a^2 = x^2 + 5ax + 6a^2$$
$$\text{Since numerator and denominator both have degree 2, divide numerator by denominator:}$$

Set up the partial fractions for the remainder term:
$$\dfrac{-ax}{(x + 2a)(x + 3a)} = \dfrac{B}{x + 2a} + \dfrac{C}{x + 3a}$$
$$-ax = B(x + 3a) + C(x + 2a)$$

Substitute $x = -2a$ to determine $B$:
$$-a(-2a) = B(-2a + 3a) + C(0) \implies 2a^2 = B(a) \implies B = 2a$$

Substitute $x = -3a$ to determine $C$:
$$-a(-3a) = B(0) + C(-3a + 2a) \implies 3a^2 = C(-a) \implies C = -3a$$

State the full partial fraction decomposition:
$$f(x) = 1 + \dfrac{2a}{x + 2a} - \dfrac{3a}{x + 3a}$$

hints: Integrate the constant and logarithmic terms from part (a) separately.
Apply −a and a, combine logarithm differences into one logarithm, and factor out a in the required form.
walkthrough:
Integrate each partial fraction from part (a):
$$\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int \left(1 + \dfrac{2a}{x + 2a} - \dfrac{3a}{x + 3a}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = x + 2a\ln(x + 2a) - 3a\ln(x + 3a)$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = a$:
$$a + 2a\ln(a + 2a) - 3a\ln(a + 3a) = a + 2a\ln(3a) - 3a\ln(4a)$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$[a - (-a)] + 2a[\ln(3a) - \ln(a)] - 3a[\ln(4a) - \ln(2a)]$$
$$= 2a + 2a\ln\left(\dfrac{3a}{a}\right) - 3a\ln\left(\dfrac{4a}{2a}\right)$$
$$= 2a + 2a\ln(3) - 3a\ln(2)$$

Combine the logarithmic terms using laws of logarithms:
$$2a\ln(3) - 3a\ln(2) = a\ln\left(3^2\right) - a\ln\left(2^3\right) = a\ln(9) - a\ln(8) = a\ln\left(\dfrac{9}{8}\right)$$

Factor out $a$ to express in the required form $a(p + \ln q)$:
$$a\left(2 + \ln\left(\dfrac{9}{8}\right)\right)$$
